scalars.scalar_value: Associate or bachelor’s degree in culinary arts, hospitality, food-service management, business administration, or related field preferred.
High school diploma, GED, or equivalent combination of education and experience required.

Minimum five years of progressively responsible food-service, culinary, restaurant, hospitality, or institutional dining experience, including significant supervisory or management responsibility. Demonstrated hands-on leadership in a high-volume kitchen is required, including directing cooks, executing standardized recipes, planning production, managing yields and portions, and assessing food quality and food safety. Experience overseeing customer service, scheduling, labor costs, employee performance, and integrated operations required. Collegiate or institutional dining and union-environment experience preferred.

items.item_text: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent combination of education and experience required. Associate or bachelor’s degree in culinary arts, hospitality, food-service management, business administration, or related field preferred. Formal culinary training or equivalent substantial hands-on culinary leadership experience required.

Minimum five years of progressively responsible food-service, culinary, restaurant, hospitality, or institutional dining experience, including significant supervisory or management responsibility. Demonstrated hands-on leadership in a high-volume kitchen is required, including directing cooks, executing standardized recipes, planning production, managing yields and portions, and assessing food quality and food safety. Experience overseeing customer service, scheduling, labor costs, employee performance, and integrated operations required. Collegiate or institutional dining and union-environment experience preferred.

1. Independently direct assigned daily shifts across front-of-house and back-of-house functions, including food production, service, cashiering, dishroom, utility, receiving, stocking, sanitation, and closing activities.

2. Assign responsibilities, establish priorities, communicate shift expectations, and verify completion of critical tasks rather than relying solely on employee reports or another manager to identify unfinished work.
3. Ensure each meal period begins with appropriate production, staffing, equipment, supplies, food-safety controls, and service readiness; conduct walkthroughs before, during, and after service.
4. Coordinate opening, meal-period transitions, handoffs, and closing; verify building security, equipment shutdown, cash-handling procedures, cleanliness, and completion of required checklists.
6. Maintain visible management presence throughout the facility and ensure effective coordination among culinary and service employees.
8. Direct and coach cooks and production employees on preparation techniques, recipe scaling, batch cooking, yields, equipment use, portioning, presentation, and service timing.

9. Prepare and adjust production plans using projected meal counts, historical participation, inventory, staffing, and equipment capacity; monitor replenishment to prevent shortages and avoid unnecessary overproduction.

10. Conduct and document quality checks before and during service, including taste, seasoning, texture, doneness, temperature, presentation, portion size, and consistency; correct deficiencies before service.

11. Verify ingredient substitutions, allergen information, dietary accommodations, labeling, and cross-contact controls with designated personnel; stop service of an affected item until uncertainty is resolved.
12. Review production records, leftovers, yields, and waste trends and recommend operational adjustments to the Executive Chef and AGM.
13. Implement culinary direction and approved recipe changes from the Executive Chef; elevate proposed menu or recipe changes for appropriate approval.
14. Oversee dining-room readiness, cashiering and point-of-sale activity, customer flow, station presentation, cleanliness, stocking, and hospitality standards throughout meal periods.
15. Monitor service quality and engage with students, faculty, staff, and guests; resolve routine concerns and follow up on recurring issues.
16. Ensure opening, transition, breakdown, and closing procedures are consistently followed and financial transactions comply with College controls.
17. Coordinate with culinary staff so food availability, labeling, service pace, and guest communication remain aligned.
18. Provide direct supervision, direction, coaching, training, evaluation, and accountability for assigned employees across operational functions.

19. Clearly communicate performance, attendance, safety, service, and conduct expectations; promptly address deficiencies and document coaching, counseling, and corrective action in coordination with HR and leadership.
20. Participate in recruitment, interviews, selection, onboarding, scheduling, evaluations, and employee development.
21. Provide station-level culinary instruction and verify employee competency in recipes, equipment, sanitation, allergens, and safe food handling.
22. Delegate work according to employee skills and classifications, monitor completion, and follow through on deficiencies; promote respectful teamwork and appropriate cross-training.
23. Prepare and adjust schedules to maintain safe, effective coverage across production and service while operating within approved labor budgets and applicable staffing requirements.
24. Assess workloads, meal counts, and operational priorities to deploy employees effectively; control avoidable overtime and unnecessary management overlap without compromising quality or safety.
25. Arrange and communicate coverage for absences, breaks, transitions, and unexpected operational demands; ensure clear supervisory handoffs.
26. Maintain accurate attendance, timekeeping, scheduling, and performance records and address exceptions promptly.
27. Apply applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement provisions and College policies consistently, coordinating employee-relations matters and union communications with HR and senior leadership.
28. Assist the AGM with operating budgets; monitor labor, food, supply, and other expenses and identify variances requiring corrective action.
29. Coordinate ordering and receiving with purchasing personnel, Chef Managers, the Executive Chef, and AGM; verify product specifications, quantities, quality, and suitability for approved recipes.
30. Maintain inventory controls, par levels, storage, rotation, labeling, security, and waste-reduction practices.
31. Use participation, production, inventory, labor, and waste data to recommend improvements in cost efficiency, productivity, and service.
32. Maintain required food-protection manager certification and ensure compliance with HACCP, College procedures, and applicable health and safety requirements.
33. Inspect production, receiving, storage, service, dining, and dishroom areas; verify required food-safety logs and corrective actions.
34. Ensure proper allergen controls, employee hygiene, cleaning, sanitation, equipment use, and safe work practices; address unsafe conditions immediately.
35. Identify facility or equipment deficiencies, initiate and follow up on work orders, and coordinate repairs with Facilities and Campus Services.

36. Coordinate closely with the AGM, Executive Chef, existing Chef Managers, Catering, Purchasing, and other Dining Services managers to maintain consistent operational standards and clear responsibilities.
37. Participate in management meetings, training, operational reviews, student engagement activities, and approved special meals and events.
38. Provide management coverage at other Dining Services locations as operationally necessary.
39. Support sustainability, food-waste reduction, service improvements, and other College priorities; perform related duties as assigned.
